title: Pfizer (PFE) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
Pfizer lifts guidance as newer drugs grow, even as COVID sales keep falling.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email[email protected]

RISKS

SUMMARY

Pfizer Inc.(PFE-2.19%)reported third-quarter 2026 results highlighting a 7% operational revenue increase in its non-COVID portfolio and 32% growth in revenues from recently launched and acquired products. Management increased full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $62 billion to $64 billion and raised adjusted earnings guidance following strong commercial performance in oncology and specialty care. The company is currently executing on a multiyear productivity initiative targeting $7.2 billion in net savings by the end of 2026 while advancing a high-priority research and development pipeline in obesity and cancer. Pfizer continues to navigate a transition period marked by upcoming patent expirations through disciplined capital allocation and the integration of strategic acquisitions like Seagen.

Francesca DeMartino:Good morning. And welcome to Pfizer's earnings call. I am Francesca DeMartino, Chief Investor Relations Officer. On behalf of the Pfizer team, thank you for joining us. This call is being made available via audio webcast at pfizer.com. Earlier this morning, we released our results for the third quarter 26 via a press release that is available on our website at pfizer.com. I am joined today by Dr. Albert Bourla, our chairman and CEO, Cecile Guegan, our CFO and Chris Boshoff, our Scientific our chief scientific officer. After their prepared remarks, we will open the call for questions. Members of our leadership team will be available for the Q&A session.

Before we get started, I want to remind you that we will be making forward looking statements and discussing certain non GAAP financial measures. I encourage you to read the disclaimers in our slide presentation the press release we issued this morning, and the disclosures in our SEC filings, which are all available on the IR website on pfizer.com. Forward looking statements on the call are subject to substantial risks and uncertainties speak only as of the call's original date, and we undertake no obligation to update or revise any of the statements. With that, I will turn the call over to Albert.

Albert Bourla:Thank you, Francesca. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our call. I am pleased with another strong quarter for Pfizer. Our excellent commercial execution, including 32% operational revenue growth in the quarter for our launched and acquired products, shows the underlying strength of our business. Financial discipline and ongoing productivity improvement are driving efficiency. And contributing favorably toward our margins. And with continued progress of our high value R&D programs, we believe that we are on a pathway to the next stage of meaningful growth. Before going further, I want to welcome Cecile Guegan, as our chief financial officer. Cecile brings more than 25 years of finance leadership and the proven ability to deliver new sources of growth.

She stood out in a global search for her expertise her deep knowledge of Pfizer, and our industry, and the strategic vision that I believe will help Pfizer unlock sustained long term value for patients and shareholders. I am looking forward to Cecile's partnership, and I am confident she could help us execute with a discipline and ambition this next chapter requires. Now let me cover several highlights of our progress in this quarter. Over the last few years, we have invested close to $80 billion in transactions that have equipped us with key products contributing to current commercial momentum, and platforms with transformative potential. About 80% of this investment was for Seagen, Metsera, Biohaven.

And we are making good progress in maximizing the value of each 1. We are pleased with the overall performance of our acquired products, which grew 37% operationally in this quarter. Our legacy Seagen portfolio grew 39% year over year in The U. S. In the quarter, driven by the strong performance of Padcev Bringing medicines together with the strength and reach of our commercial organization, has deepened our presence in the oncology community. We now offer physicians and care teams a broader set of options and more expertise helping patients and driving growth for Pfizer. Seagen did more than strengthen our commercial position.

It also expanded our ability to discover oncology breakthroughs, doubling the size of our early stage pipeline at the time we close the acquisition. In our late stage development programs, we are advancing potential antibody drug conjugates that could bring meaningful improvements for patients with cancer. I am pleased with the pace of progress over the past year with our expansive clinical development program across our obesity portfolio. We plan to advance 10 active and planned Phase 3 trials in 2026. Including 1 evaluating a switch from approved weekly therapies to our investigational monthly GLP-1 peptide berobenatide.

We have made significant progress with enrollment across our pivotal berobenatide program, as well as our amylin combination program where our Phase 2b study is now fully enrolled. We are working toward the first in a series of potential approvals for berobenatide in 2028. With planning of our go-to-market strategy, well underway. Biohaven also has been a strategically important addition for Pfizer. In the quarter, grew by 33% operationally, driven by underlying demand and excellent commercial execution. We see real opportunity to help patients with migraine, and for the oral CGRP class to be a key growth driver. Even as we manage market dynamics in a competitive field.

We are leading the oral CGRP class in The US, and are working to extend that position internationally. We are seeing international growth as more patients can now get this treatment in key countries, including The UK, Italy, and Japan. We are also encouraged by strong adoption when we are able to expand access. 2026 execution in R&D has been strong. And we continue to prioritize the highest value opportunities for patients and future growth across our 4 therapeutic focus areas. Our excellent progress showcases our momentum in advanced our strategy, recent months, we achieved 2 key regulatory decisions, 1 key pivotal readout and 8 key pivotal study starts. Alongside strong data we presented at several recent medical congresses.

We are excited by the pipeline of opportunities in areas of strategic focus and commercial strength. This includes late stage programs across tumor types in oncology, including multiple myeloma breast cancer, and lung cancer. Within inflammation and immunology, and, of course, in pneumococcal vaccines. Chris will share more detail about our recent advancement in the recent months. Pipeline strategy is grounded in disciplined prioritization and accelerated execution. And we are confident that we are advancing our most significant opportunities for future patient impact and growth. Today, we are raising our guidance for full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted earnings per share. This reflects our strong performance through the third quarter and confidence in our ability to execute our strategy.

Along with our financial discipline and the progress we continue to make with our R&D pipeline, we believe Pfizer is well positioned to drive growth towards the end of the decade and create sustained value for patients and shareholders over the long term. We have deployed AI in our business with the goal of improving efficiency in manufacturing and sharpening how we engage physicians and patients. In R&D, we are working to accelerate innovation with faster target validation and better molecule and biomarker selection. The recent launch of our new product in over 120 countries. Genesis takes on the administrative burden so our safety scientists can spend their time where it matters most.

Assessing causality, detecting safety signals, and protecting patients. With that, I will turn it over to Cecile.

Cecile Guegan:Thank you, Albert, and good morning. I am proud to speak to you today as Pfizer's CFO. I am looking forward to continuing to work alongside the executive leadership team and lead a world class finance organization. I am genuinely excited about what we can achieve together and I will approach this role with financial discipline and a focus on translating Pfizer's scientific and commercial progress into durable shareholder value. I am confident in our strategy and that as a team, we can deliver durable long term value for our shareholders with rigorous capital allocation and disciplined execution. Now I am pleased to share our third quarter results. Which demonstrate continuous commercial execution and financial discipline.

Revenues from our non COVID product delivered solid growth while product mix productivity and cost management supported margin expansion and enabled continuous investment across our robust pipeline. This year's performance gives us the confidence to raise our full year 26 revenue guidance as well as raise and narrow our adjusted diluted EPS guidance. Now on to the results. Third quarter 26 revenue of $617 billion came in ahead of our expectation. With strong 7% operational revenue growth of our non COVID products. Driven by key brands in The U. S, and select international markets. Offset by lower revenues from our COVID-19 products.

On the bottom line, third quarter 26 reported diluted EPS was $0.56 In addition, adjusted diluted EPS of $0.87 exceeded our expectation. And includes the $0.10 charge related to the Innovent transaction. This outperformance reflects cost discipline and improved productivity across the organization. Even as we increase investment towards future growth drivers and advance several Phase 3 study starts. We saw solid revenue contributions in the quarter, from Eliquis, Padcev, the Vyndaqel family NURTEC, and Lorbrena. While our COVID-19 products the Paxlovid family declined in the quarter. Our launched and acquired product contributed $3.8 billion in revenues. And grew 32% operationally in the quarter, primarily driven by Padcev of $255 million NURTEC $135 million and Lorbrena, $114 million.

We continue to invest behind this group of products to mitigate LOE headwinds over the next several years. In addition, this quarter's performance demonstrates clear progress against our objective of returning to growth towards the end of the decade. Cost discipline and continued optimization across the company including our manufacturing footprint, remain priorities. We are making meaningful progress with our productivity initiatives and remain on track to deliver nearly all of the anticipated $7.2 billion of net savings by the end of 26 for ongoing cost improvement programs. As we announced last quarter, we are initiating the next phase of these programs to deliver an anticipated additional $2.5 billion of net cost savings from 2027 through 2029.

These savings support increased operating efficiency and contribute favorably to our margins. At the same time, we continue to prioritize investment in pipeline programs that we believe have the greatest potential to deliver meaningful breakthroughs for patients and create long term value for our shareholders. Adjusted gross margin for the third quarter was 77%. Primarily reflecting favorable product mix and continued cost management. When we look at the components of our adjusted operating expenses of $6.8 billion, Adjusted SI&A expenses increased 2% operationally reflecting in part an increase due to a lower favorable adjustment of US healthcare reform fees year over year offset partially by lower targeted marketing and promotional investments toward growth drivers and ongoing cost productivity. Improvements.

Adjusted R&D expenses increased 18% operationally which includes planned investment in priority oncology and obesity programs including several Phase 3 study starts. An acquired in progress R and D decreased 52% operationally primarily reflecting a $650 million charge related to the Innovent transaction this quarter compared to a $1.35 billion charge in the prior year quarter. Related to the 3S Bio transaction. Third quarter 26 adjusted operating margin was 36%. Reflecting effective cost management strong non COVID revenue performance, higher investment in the business and I will note was tempered by the AIPR&D charge related to the Innovent transaction. As I mentioned earlier, third quarter adjusted diluted EPS was $0.87.

Based on our year to date performance, including continued growth across our non COVID product, and disciplined execution we are raising our full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $1.5 billion at the midpoint to a range of $62 billion to $64 billion We are reaffirming our expectation of approximately $4 billion for the COVID products with the majority of the Comirnatio revenues expected in the fourth quarter consistent with the vaccination season. Vaxillary utilization will continue to be influenced by infection rates and treatment demand.

In addition, we now expect full-year 2026 R&D expense to be in the range of $10.8 billion to $11.8 billion We are raising and narrowing our full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to a range of $2.95 to $3.05. This represents an increase of $0.10 at the midpoint while absorbing the $0.10 per share impact of the Innovent transaction. We are reaffirming all other components of our financial guide. Our updated outlook reflects our confidence in a non COVID product progress across our cost improvement initiative. Expectation of full year adjusted gross margin in the mid-70% percent range and continued investment in our priority pipeline programs. Turning to capital allocation. Our capital allocation priorities remain unchanged.

Reinvest in the business at appropriate returns maintain and, over time, grow our dividend. And deliver shareholder returns while preserving flexibility for future value enhancing actions. Including share repurchases. Following the Innovent transaction, which closed in the third quarter, our current BD capacity is approximately $6 billion In the first 9 months of 2026, we invested $9.2 billion in internal and external R&D, and returned $7.3 billion to shareholders through our quarterly dividend. Our third quarter year to date 2026 operating cash flow was $8.8 billion and leverage ended the quarter at 2.6x slightly below our 2026 target of 2.7x.

Given the impact of upcoming LOEs, we expect leverage to remain around current levels, or modestly higher during the LOE transition period. We remain focused on maintaining a strong financial position while continuing to invest in innovation and support shareholder returns. In conclusion, I want to leave you with 2 key takeaways. First, operational excellence. The non COVID product continued to perform well, growing 7% operationally. And our launched and acquired product grew 32% operationally. Providing further evidence of our strong capabilities and consistent execution. Second, financial discipline. We are improving operating efficiency while enabling increased pipeline investment in programs which we believe offer the greatest potential for patients and shareholders.

Together, this performance demonstrates that we are executing our strategy managing the upcoming LOE transition, and strengthening the foundation for a return to growth towards the end of the decade. With that, I will turn it over to Chris.

Chris Boshoff FMedSci:Thanks, Cecile. Across our 4 therapeutic areas, we made strong progress last quarter. I will provide color on recent developments in these programs, starting with Elrexfio, our internally discovered BCMA bispecific, which has now delivered 2 positive Phase 3 readouts in double class exposed multiple myeloma. Most recently, in MM32, Elrexfio monotherapy demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression free survival versus in investigator's choice of 3 established standard of care regimens.

This is important because the choice of 3 standard of care regimens provides a robust representation of how c d 38 refractory multiple myeloma is treated today in a patient population that is growing as anti c d 38 therapy moves in the first line setting. And the results themselves were strong. At the time of the interim analysis, more than 75% of patients receiving Elrexfio had not experienced disease progression or death from any cause, and the estimated 18-month progression free survival rate was approximately 68%. Safety in 32 was consistent with Elrexfio's known profile and also potentially differentiated.

With infection prophylaxis measures incorporated from the start of 32, rates of grade 3 or higher infections lower than those observed in MagnetisMM-5, Elrexfio's 1st positive pivotal trial in double class exposed multiple myeloma. For context, such infection prophylaxis measures were not in place at the start of 5. These were instituted following early deaths due to infections that were concentrated in China and 2 other countries during a COVID wave impacting the overall hazard ratio of MagnetisMM-5. 5 data expected at a medical meeting before year end and will provide further information on efficacy and safety. Taken together, these positive phase 3 results from MM32 and 5 strengthen our confidence in moving Elrexfio into earlier lines of treatment.

We are building a compelling case of fixed dose Elrexfio monotherapy from first relapse regardless of prior CD38 exposure. And with additional pivotal studies in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma underway, Elrexfio's eligible patient population could grow approximately 5-fold pending clinical and regulatory success. Moving next to atermaciclib. Our potential first in class highly selective CDK4 inhibitor. Building on the leadership we established with Ibrance, we are advancing atermaciclib as a potential next generation backbone for first line and early HR positive breast cancer. Our KAT6 inhibitor, mevrometostat, is being developed in later line settings. Atermaciclib was designed in house to improve upon CDK4/6 inhibitors. The current standard of care backbone for HR positive breast cancer.

A key limitation of this class is safety and tolerability with CDK 6 in inhibition being a key contributor to adverse events. We designed atermaciclib to maximize efficacy through greater CDK 4 inhibition while improving tolerability by minimizing CDK 6 engagement. Atermaciclib is 33x more selective for CDK4 versus CDK6 comparing favorably versus the standard of care. Here are 2 datasets fueling enthusiasm for atermaciclib. On the left are data presented at ESMO from the Phase 2 FOURLIGHT-1 study of atermaciclib plus fulvestrant in patients with HR positive HER 2 negative breast cancer. All participants had previously received a CDK4/6 inhibitor and notably 92% of the atermaciclib participants were randomized within 3 months of discontinuing a CDK4/6 inhibitor.

The atermaciclib regimen reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 40% compared to investigator choice of fulvestrant or everolimus plus exemestane. These results in a population with highly refractory or resistant disease increase our confidence in our ongoing Phase 3 trial of atermaciclib versus investigator's choice of CDK4/6 inhibitor in the first line setting. On the right are data from atermaciclib's Phase 2 study in early breast cancer. With a combination of atermaciclib plus letrozole, 88% of participants' tumors demonstrated complete cell cycle arrest compared to only 18% versus letrozole alone.

These results support our plan to combine atermaciclib with a selective estrogen receptor degrader, giredestrant, in a Phase 3 early breast cancer trial expected to initiate within the next few months. This study design has been aligned with regulators building on the expected approval of giredestrant in this setting. This slide shows FOURLIGHT-1 safety and tolerability data alongside results from pivotal studies of the 3 approved CDK4/6 inhibitors plus fulvestrant. These are cross trial comparisons Therefore, definitive conclusions cannot be drawn. These data further suggest that high CDK4 selectivity drives improved safety and tolerability, enabling continuous dosing excellent adherence, and potentially great efficacy.

Grade 3 or higher neutropenia was numerically lower with atermaciclib than with any of the approved agents, with no grade 4 or 5 neutropenia reported. Any grade diarrhea was lower than with a abemaciclib, and comparable to palbociclib and ribociclib. Dose with reductions due to adverse events were 14% with atermaciclib compared to 32 to 43 percent with the approved agents. Turning to tivonatinib. We are advancing an extensive program for this potentially best in class PD-1/VEGF bicyclist. Antibody with over 1.2 thousand patients treated globally and a consistent safety profile. This includes 2 ongoing Phase 3 trials with 2 additional Phase 3 trials expected to begin this year.

Updated results at ESMO strengthen our confidence as we expand tivonatinib's development since SITC 25 confirmed response rate for the pivotal dose of tivonatinib plus doublet chemotherapy from the ongoing Phase 2 study have risen by roughly 20 percentage points in nonsquamous and squamous first line non small cell lung cancer. They now stand at approximately 80% exceeding those of tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in this study. Median progressive free survival was nearly 14 months for both histologies. An improvement of roughly 4 to 5 months versus the comparators. Notably, tislelizumab's efficacy was consistent with historical Phase 3 results for the leading PD 1 antibody pembrolizumab. Which supports the relevance of the control arms.

We are also encouraged by how tivonatinib efficacy and safety results compared with Phase 3 data for the PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, ivonesimab. While recognizing the limitations of cross trial comparisons. Now for I&I. Tilrekimig, a potential first in class trispecific antibody, tilrekimig, was designed in house to simultaneously target multiple complementary drivers of type 2 inflammation IL 4 IL 13, and TSLP. Phase 2 results in atopic dermatitis provide compelling proof of concept. At the top monthly doses, tilrekimig treatment led to placebo adjusted response rate of about 50% for EASI-75, defined as a 75% or greater improvement in the eczema area and severity index.

While cross trial comparisons have limitations, these Phase 2 data suggest the potential for superiority over dupilumab the current standard-of-care biologic. These secondary endpoints in our ongoing Phase 3 program are powered to test this hypothesis in a head to head setting. For safety, Tilrekimig demonstrated a favorable profile. At subcutaneous doses up to 400 milligrams once every 4 weeks the observed frequency of conjunctivitis and injection site reactions were lower than rates reported with dupilumab and comparable to placebo. Beyond atopic dermatitis, tilrekimig offers a pipeline and a product opportunity. Targeting pathways that are validated by approved therapies across 9 different diseases, Late stage studies are underway in severe asthma and moderate to severe COPD.

Moving to our potential best in class pneumococcal conjugate vaccine program, building on Prefna's 25 plus year legacy of effectiveness and safety we are advancing next-generation candidates designed for leading serotype and invasive disease coverage. In pediatrics, PCV 25 delivered strong phase 2 results All 20 serotypes shared with Prefna 20 met the 2 fold post dose I post dose 4 IgG criterion historically used to establish non inferiority. Since the pediatric licensure of Prevnar 20 in 2020, the FDA established an updated, more stringent 1.5-fold non inferiority criterion that is incorporated into our Phase 3 design.

Given the Phase 2 results and tighter confidence intervals expected with a much larger sample size in Phase 3, modeling predicts this criterion will be met for at least 22 of 25 serotypes in our pivotal study. Taken together with seroresponse data, functional opsonophagocytic activity (OPA) titers, and the totality of evidence approach to licensure. These results provide confidence as we aim to deliver a best in class pediatric pneumococcal vaccine protecting against serotypes that collectively cause an estimated 84% of invasive disease cases in US children under 5. This would represent an incremental increase of approximately 25 percentage points versus 20. Our Phase 3 program is well underway.

With the Phase 3 lot to lot consistency study already fully enrolled. In adults, PCV35 extends the enhanced serotype 3 technology we validated with PCV25 to other key serotypes. With a Phase 1 start expected this year. Looking ahead, we expect a strong cadence of regulatory decisions data readouts, and pivotal study starts over the next 12 months. These include a readout from MEVPRO-1, which based on the current event rate is now expected in the first quarter of 27. If successful, MEVPRO-1 could support approval for mevrometostat, our in house discovered potential first in class EZH 2 inhibitor for prostate cancer. Expanding our franchise. With that, I will hand it back to Albert.

Albert Bourla:Thank you, Chris. And in closing, operational excellence is driving a commercial momentum across our key growth brands. And I would say, importantly, with our launched and acquired products. Our capital allocation strategy, on the other hand, is designed to create long term shareholder value. And our late stage pipeline progress with a significant number of pivotal readouts expected near term is strengthening our opportunity to extend our leadership in key areas. And make a difference for patients. I am confident Pfizer is well positioned for growth towards the end of this decade and for long-term shareholder value creation.

We have line of sight to our aim of delivering a risk adjusted high single digit revenue CAGR from year-end 2028 through year-end 2033. Now we will move to Q and A. And operator, please assemble the queue.

Chris Schott:Great. Thanks so much for the questions. I just had 2 pipeline ones. Maybe first on the trispecific, tilrekimig, How are you thinking about the positioning of this 1 in atopic derm as we consider, I guess, first line versus second line usage as maybe we just think about the very strong data you presented versus a very well entrenched standard of care And maybe just a second part of that, just talk about the timelines for the indications beyond AD that you are pursuing? The second question was then just pivoting over to the upcoming Phase 1/2a amylin and combo data that we are going to see.

Here, can you just help some set some expectations about how you are thinking about that data and then the type of titration schedule that is being used in that study just to help us kind of frame out what we are going to see with that with that readout? Thanks so much.

Albert Bourla:No. Thank you. Chris, would you like to cover the timelines of tilrekimig and, of course, the amylin and the berobenatide questions? Then maybe, Alexandre, you can speak a little bit about the commercial positioning.

Chris Boshoff FMedSci:Thank you very much for the question. So as you know, we have now started the Phase 3 program for tilrekimig. In atopic dermatitis, 2 studies. 1 of those studies include a head to head against dupilumab, and we also started the Phase 2/3 study, a continuous design for COPD and Phase 3 studies for severe asthma with expected readouts in 2028 and 2029. Regarding the amylin GLP-1, as you are aware, the SOLIS 1 study is now completely recruited. That is the robustly designed Phase 2b study, SOLIS-1, of lotiglipron, single agent, and danuglipron plus in different doses and different titrations. We expect the readout for that study for efficacy the second half of 27.

The ongoing Phase 1/2a study we will give an update at end of this year recognizing that study was designed for safety And PK clinical pharmacology, not for efficacy. Thank you.

Albert Bourla:And then what about the positioning of the--how do you think about that?

Alexandre de Germay:Chris, thanks for the questions. I think we all know that this is a very large category. What we have learned with our and overall dermatology franchises, there is a lot of patients profile that requires different type of therapy. And we see that very much with the JAK versus the biologics, and we see that there are some patients that actually move from 1 to the other to drop off. There is a lot of circulation of those patients. We are building capabilities across US and we see that we are making good progress.

So for instance, as you saw in this quarter, in international, we reached, like, 100 million combined between our 2 assets in dermatologists for the quarter. So we start having a nice phase And as I said, as we move into the result of the study, we will be able to actually cap some of those lapsed patients and naive patients with a very specific profile that we are defining. So first in class, strong efficacy, and clearly unmet medical need in this category.

Albert Bourla:Thank you very much. Next question, please.

Operator:Our next question comes from David Risinger with Leerink Partners. Please go ahead.

Dave Risinger:And I wanted to say congratulations to Cecile on your new role as CFO of Pfizer and look forward to working with you. My question is on U. S. Net price. In the third quarter and going forward. Could you comment on any gross to net benefits to net sales in the third quarter, including from any 340B-related upside. And discuss US net price prospects looking forward in the near term? Thank you.

Cecile Guegan:Thanks very much. First, for your good wishes. So as it relates to the pricing in Q3, with the exception of, as we were expecting, the impact on Eliquis which started in, Q3, of the January wholesale acquisition cost (WAC) price decrease I would say there is not really any very material change into our gross-to-net Dynamics during the third quarter. So the performance that we are seeing is, for most part, driven by strong market performance and volume rather than dynamics around the gross-to-net. As we are looking into, the future, obviously, not commenting today on 2027.

But we will obviously reflect into our guidance for 2027, the various dynamics that we are seeing being IRA with 2 of our product entering the negotiation program in 2027 and any of the dynamics around, the 340B impact and changes, including as a credit rebate model implemented starting in January and also, obviously, some of the MFN impacts that we have following the agreements we have with the government. But that is a summary. it is a performance into Q3 is really a reflection of the strong execution rather than, dynamics around gross-to-net that would have been contributing.

Albert Bourla:Very well. Thank you very much. Next question, please.

Operator:Our next question comes from Umer Raffat with Evercore ISI. Your line is now open.

Umer Raffat:Hi, guys. Thanks for taking my question. Albert, there is clearly been a lot of progress on SG and A improvements over the last couple of years and I acknowledge that. it is not step function, but there is been improvement. But then I recall David before he moved on, had mentioned, that majority of the total net cost savings of $7.2 billion will be delivered by the end of 26. So when I look now back at the Pfizer p and l, I am seeing SG&A and R&D was about $24.5 billion back in 2022. it is about the same in 2026 as well.

And I acknowledge R and D has gone up a bit as SG&A has come back a bit. But the broader dynamics on OpEx are still broadly in that $24 billion to $25 billion camp. And I guess, how do you think about that heading into the dividend integrity, the cost lever heading into patent expiries? Thank you.

Cecile Guegan:Cecile, why do not you take this question? Yes. So as I mentioned earlier, we are on track to delivering the $7.2 billion of savings that we had implemented as part of our first phase of the cost improvement programs. Those savings were in different places. it is 1 in our manufacturing footprint for cost, 2 in R&D, but reinvested And we are indeed increasing our R&D investment in order to support the pipeline product and programs that we have in addition to, obviously, the acquisition that we made And then on the SI&A side coming from the commercial and marketing expenses, as well as G&A.

So what we are seeing today in our operating expenses I would then relate to just the third quarter, which had some onetime dynamics that drove SI&A up. We are still expecting based on guidance, we will see a decline in SI&A versus last year. So that is the first piece that I would say. Going forward, we have announced our second phase of the program with a $2.5 billion of savings. Both in SG and A and in our cost of manufacturing. Those will translate into savings. So we are expecting to see those translating and mitigating the margin erosion as part of the LOE transition in 2027 to 2029.

Albert Bourla:Thank you very, very much, Yusuf. Next question.

Operator:We will go next to Akash Tewari with Jefferies. Your line is now open.

Akash Tewari:Hey, thanks so much. Just a couple. I know in the spring, you had a kind of 45- to 50-patient biomarker analysis on your oral STAT6 and you were going to make a decision on whether to go from Stage 1 to Stage 2. Is there an update on that program and really how do you think about target engagement and biomarker reduction to what we have seen with some of the degraders? And then on your GLP-1/amylin, I think your Phase 1/2, you just updated on clinical trials to 201 patients. I think it was originally planned to be closer to 400 Any color on what drove that decision with the amylin GLP-1 combo with Metsera? Thank you.

Chris Boshoff FMedSci:Chris, both question goes to you. Okay. So thank you very much. So the question on STAT6, potentially first in class, oral STAT6 program. Thanks for the question. This is an area very important for us for the I&I portfolio. As we previously stated, we have adapted the program to incorporate some additional DDI studies. So we should give you a readout for the STAT6 later this year. Regarding the Amylin and berubenatide, as I stated earlier, the SOLIS-1 study is fully recruited. That study is for efficacy reading out end of next year and the Phase 1/2a study was adapted for the additional PK studies we are doing. But there is nothing really nothing material changes to the trial.

Albert Bourla:Thank you. Next question, please.

Operator:We will go next to Vamil Divan with Guggenheim. Your line is now open.

Vamil Divan:Great. Thanks for taking my questions. Again, maybe on the pipeline. 1, we noticed that you posted a new Phase 1 trial for your PI 3 k inhibitor on ct.gov last week. Heard what you said around atermaciclib in your KAT6. Curious if you can maybe just talk about how you see that asset sort of fitting into your broader breast cancer strategy. Then the other question may be coming from ESMO. We saw the VOLGA data that AstraZeneca released that could suggest maybe less need for the use of fewer cycles of Padcev in patients with bladder cancer.

Curious if you have any user reactions to that data set or how it might impact how you think the use of PADCEV may play out in the future.

Chris Boshoff FMedSci:Yes.
